candidates.name: New-York-Airbnb-Listings-2024
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSV `new_york_listings_2024.csv` — NYC Airbnb listings as of 5 Jan 2024, sourced from Kaggle (vrindakallu/new-york-dataset). This snapshot date falls squarely inside the missing 2023-06→2024-03 Local Law 18 window (post-enforcement, ~4 months after the 5 Sep 2023 registration deadline). Data loaded into a SQLite3 db and visualized in Power BI (.pbix template also in repo). 24 commits, no license stated.
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap #1 (NYC dumps 2023-06→2024-03 missing from Inside Airbnb's CDN) with an actual point-in-time NYC listings snapshot from inside that window; can be cross-checked against the pre/post LL18 listing-count collapse (22,246→4,000) the team already knows about.
candidates.size_hint: unspecified row count, single CSV + SQLite db

candidates.name: New York Airbnb Open Data 2024 (Kaggle)
candidates.what_it_holds: Original Kaggle source for the same 5 Jan 2024 NYC Airbnb listings snapshot mirrored into the Tracey-Sneed GitHub repo above; https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vrindakallu/new-york-dataset
candidates.why_useful: Same value as the GitHub mirror (fills the LL18-window NYC gap); listed separately since it's the canonical host and may carry more metadata/columns than the GitHub copy.

candidates.name: U.S. Airbnb Open Data (AB_US_2023.csv)
candidates.what_it_holds: Kaggle-hosted compilation of Inside Airbnb US-city listings recompiled/updated 14 Apr 2023 as `AB_US_2023.csv` (host id, listing id, name, lat/lon, neighbourhood, price, room type, min nights, reviews, availability, city column covering multiple US metros including New York City).
candidates.why_useful: A US multi-city, single-file snapshot from April 2023 — a few months before Local Law 18 enforcement (5 Sep 2023) — giving a clean 'last normal' NYC cross-section to pair with the post-enforcement Jan 2024 snapshot above for a before/after comparison without needing the missing CDN dumps.
candidates.size_hint: multi-city CSV, tens of thousands of rows (typical Inside Airbnb compilation size)
candidates.license: Kaggle dataset license (unspecified); source data CC0-derivative per Inside Airbnb terms
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: partially overlaps the 13-city Inside Airbnb panel already held, but this specific April-2023 pre-LL18 US compilation is not confirmed already in hand

candidates.name: New York City Airbnb 2023, Public Data (Kaggle)
candidates.what_it_holds: Kaggle dataset titled 'New York City Airbnb 2023, Public Data'; exact snapshot date and row count could not be confirmed via fetch (page content not retrievable through the tool), but title and Kaggle notebook activity (July 2023) suggest a mid-2023 NYC snapshot, potentially inside or just before the LL18 gap window.
candidates.why_useful: Possible additional NYC 2023 point-in-time snapshot; worth a follow-up direct check (browser or Kaggle API) to confirm the exact scrape date before treating as filling the gap.
candidates.last_activity: dataset referenced by a July 2023 Kaggle notebook

candidates.name: airbnb-market-data (tmasjc)
candidates.what_it_holds: R/Shiny app plus a `download_csv.R` command-line tool that pulls Inside Airbnb 'listings.csv' (summary) files directly from data.insideairbnb.com for any city/date Inside Airbnb has archived; two cities (Berlin, Vienna) pre-committed as CSVs in-repo (e.g. Vienna Mar–Sep 2017), other cities downloadable on demand. 43 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A reusable, generic method to pull whatever historical snapshots Inside Airbnb still exposes for a given city/date, which could be pointed at any surviving NYC dates near the LL18 window or used as a template for building a systematic archive puller; not NYC-specific itself.
candidates.time_coverage: depends on what Inside Airbnb has archived per city
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: method overlaps existing team scraping of Inside Airbnb but this is an independent public implementation

candidates.name: Data-Pipeline-for-analyzing-Inside-Airbnb-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Airflow/S3/Spark/EMR/Redshift/Athena pipeline that ingests Inside Airbnb listings data 'at scale' for community analysis; no committed data files, pulls from insideairbnb.com at run time.
candidates.why_useful: Infrastructure pattern for bulk-pulling and warehousing Inside Airbnb data across many cities/dates if the team wants to industrialize its own historical-vintage capture; not itself a data source.

candidates.name: AirbnbDataPipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache Airflow ETL pipeline (to Redshift) for Inside Airbnb data covering Boston, New York, and Seattle 'for the past three years'; pipeline code only, no data files committed to the repo. 17 commits, no license.
candidates.why_useful: Another reusable pipeline pattern specifically naming New York among its target cities; low value on its own since it holds no data and depends on Inside Airbnb's live (non-archival) CDN.
candidates.time_coverage: N/A (pipeline only, pulls whatever is currently on insideairbnb.com)

candidates.name: nycOpenData (rOpenSci)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package giving programmatic access to any NYC Open Data Socrata dataset (search/filter/download), including the city's own short-term-rental registration dataset published by the Mayor's Office of Special Enforcement under Local Law 18.
candidates.why_useful: Generic but working method to pull NYC's OSE short-term-rental registration counts/records over time (registrations fell from ~38,000 at start of 2023 to ~3,000 by 2026), which is a direct, point-in-time-able proxy for NYC STR supply through the LL18 transition — complements rather than duplicates Inside Airbnb listing snapshots.
candidates.geography: New York City (any NYC Open Data dataset)
candidates.time_coverage: live pull; historical depth depends on dataset revision history on the portal
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: adjacent to, not the same as, the existing '25 municipal STR registries incl. NYC OSE' holding — this is a generic access tool rather than a stored NYC OSE dataset

candidates.name: sodapy-tutorial-nyc-opendata
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/sodapy tutorial demonstrating pulls from the NYC Open Data Socrata API, generically applicable to the OSE short-term-rental registration dataset or any other NYC dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Lower-friction Python alternative to the R nycOpenData package for the same NYC OSE registration pull; marginal beyond that package.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same purpose as ropensci/nycOpenData candidate above

candidates.name: strr (UPGo McGill)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (422 commits) with functions to clean raw AirDNA-format short-term-rental data, detect commercial/multi-listing operators and 'ghost hostels', compress/expand daily-status tables, and estimate listing locations (`strr_process_*`, `strr_multi`, `strr_ghost`, `strr_FREH`, `strr_raffle`). Operates on user-supplied AirDNA files; no data committed. No visible license.
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, published toolkit for exactly the realised-occupancy/commercial-operator questions in gap #2 (AirDNA-style exports) and for classifying professional vs. casual hosts — useful if the team ever obtains an AirDNA sample or Inside Airbnb calendar data and wants a vetted commercial-listing / ghost-hostel detector rather than building one from scratch; academically used by McGill's Urban Politics and Governance lab in several STR housing-impact papers, including work touching NYC-style regulation questions.
candidates.geography: generic (used in Montreal, Toronto, Los Angeles, New York studies by the same lab)
candidates.time_coverage: N/A (processing toolkit, not a stored dataset)

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub: no repo was found that stores an actual Inside Airbnb NYC dump timestamped inside 2023-06–2024-03, and no GitHub mirror of pre-2023 Inside Airbnb archives turned up despite several targeted queries (Inside Airbnb itself confirms its CDN only keeps ~1 year and that older data requires a manual request, consistent with what the team already knows). The two best finds are Kaggle-hosted NYC snapshots dated 2023-04-14 (pre-enforcement, US-wide) and 2024-01-05 (post-enforcement, NYC-only, also mirrored on GitHub by Tracey-Sneed) which bracket the LL18 transition even though neither sits exactly inside the missing window — worth pulling both to at least get a coarse before/after cross-section. Excluded as not-new: the many repos re-analysing the well-known Kaggle 'AB_NYC_2019' file (chris-leonard, karlyndiary — no raw data committed anyway, DeepakKumarGS, sevesilvestre, otavio-s-s, gurezende, Ajitesh27, NikhilKumarMutyala, Aafrakhan) and generic Airbnb.com scraper repos (oxylabs, digital-engineering, dtrungtin, databooter) which are out of scope both as duplicates and as tools that would scrape airbnb.com directly (a ToS decision, not ours to run). The 2024 hedonic-pricing paper on Local Law 18 price competition (Tourism Management journal, tandfonline) has no visible public replication package/GitHub/OSF link. Also worth a later look by another scout: searching specifically for GitHub Actions-based 'daily snapshot' repos of the NYC OSE STR registration list (append-only commit history), which would be a genuinely new point-in-time series if one exists — none was found in this pass.
